grounded_facts: Logan Marlowe confronts Darian Calloway, accusing him of wasting time and asserting that he doesn't know what he's doing.
memories.memory_text: I remember Logan Marlowe telling me I was wasting time and didn’t know what I was doing, yelling at me while I tried to focus on Taylor Hawthorne.

memories.memory_text: I told Logan Marlowe to shut up and get out of my way so I could focus on helping Taylor Hawthorne instead of dealing with him.

grounded_facts: Darian Calloway talks to Taylor Hawthorne throughout the procedure to reassure her, sharing personal reflections to ease tension and maintain connection.
memories.memory_text: I talked to Taylor Hawthorne the whole time to keep her calm, telling her she seemed like a good kid and sharing how I've had years of bad luck with my house, car, and wife, hoping it would help her feel less scared even though I'd never done anything like this before.

grounded_facts: A tense The Midwinter Meeting occurs in the Anonymous Screenplay 57 between Darian Calloway, Logan Marlowe, and Taylor Hawthorne, during which medical aid is administered under duress.
memories.memory_text: I was in the Anonymous Screenplay 57 with Logan Marlowe and Taylor Hawthorne, and I could feel the tension rising as I dropped to my knees to help her—tying the tubing, filling the syringe, giving her the shot, all while under pressure and knowing we had no room for error.

grounded_facts: Darian Calloway successfully gives Taylor Hawthorne a glucagon injection using the kit, following improvised instructions from her weak responses and his own limited knowledge from TV.
memories.memory_text: I dropped to my knees beside Taylor Hawthorne and opened the pouch to get the syringe and other supplies, using what little I knew from TV to give her the glucagon shot, and I made sure to pull her sleeve back down after it was done.

grounded_facts: Darian Calloway uses a specialized drill to open the floor the glass notebook in the Anonymous Screenplay 57.
memories.memory_text: I used a specialized drill to work on opening the floor the glass notebook, sparks flying as I focused on the task.

grounded_facts: Logan Marlowe sarcastically downplays Darian Calloway's achievement in saving someone's life.
memories.memory_text: Logan Marlowe told me, 'Congratulations. You saved her life for ten minutes,' and I looked up at him, not sure what he meant by that.

memories.memory_text: I saw two uniformed cops on the the weathered jacket at the front stoop, and I knew they were there because someone had called the police.

memories.memory_text: I saw Noel Wilder look up at the security camera in the foyer and mime that she would take care of the police interaction.

memories.memory_text: I saw Noel Wilder reposition Sidney Cavendish out of view and put the the blue radio in his lap, making sure he was ready but hidden in case the police came in.

grounded_facts: Noel Wilder whispers strict instructions to Sidney Cavendish not to speak, enforcing operational silence during the police encounter.
memories.memory_text: I inferred that Noel Wilder whispered strict instructions to Sidney Cavendish not to speak, keeping everything silent during the police encounter.

grounded_facts: Sidney Cavendish reveals he called the police, leading to their sudden arrival at the door, which shifts Noel Wilder's situation from hidden crisis to immediate external threat.
memories.memory_text: I saw Noel Wilder looking up at the camera and miming that she'd take care of the police, but I wasn't sure if she actually had a plan or if she was just trying to keep us calm.

grounded_facts: Noel Wilder uses miming toward the security camera to convey that she will handle the police, calming Darian Calloway’s fears.
memories.memory_text: I inferred that Noel Wilder was trying to calm me down by miming she’d handle the police, though I wasn’t entirely sure how she’d do it.

grounded_facts: Logan Marlowe realizes Noel Wilder and Taylor Hawthorne saw his face, raising the risk of identification.
memories.memory_text: I inferred that Logan Marlowe must be worried because Noel Wilder and Taylor Hawthorne saw his face, which could mean they identify him later.

grounded_facts: Logan Marlowe informs Darian Calloway that Noel Wilder and Taylor Hawthorne saw his face, implying a serious risk.
memories.memory_text: Logan Marlowe told me that she saw his face, and the kid did too, so he was concerned about being recognized.

grounded_facts: Darian Calloway downplays the significance of Logan Marlowe being seen, creating interpersonal tension.
memories.memory_text: I told Logan Marlowe that his problem with being seen wasn't mine, and I didn't let it affect my focus.

grounded_facts: Logan Marlowe tells Darian Calloway that being present implicates him in a crime, and that one offense binds him to all, implying unavoidable consequences.
memories.memory_text: Logan Marlowe told me that just being there with him puts me on the hook for one crime, and that drags me into all the rest—he made it clear there's no walking away, no matter how much I want out.

grounded_facts: Noel Wilder hears Logan Marlowe threatening Darian Calloway, implying they are already involved in a crime and will be held responsible for more.
memories.memory_text: I didn't realize Noel Wilder was listening at first, but she heard everything—Logan Marlowe threatening me, saying my presence ties me to all the crimes, and she was left horrified by what she overheard.

grounded_facts: Darian Calloway expresses strong disbelief or rejection of the current situation, indicating resistance to the unfolding events.
memories.memory_text: I said 'Bullshit' because I refused to accept what was happening.

grounded_facts: Logan Marlowe asserts control and escalates tension by implying a predetermined, threatening outcome in his communication with Taylor Hawthorne.
memories.memory_text: I heard Logan Marlowe say 'You know how this gotta end,' and I could feel him trying to control the situation with that threat.

memories.memory_text: I kept drilling with the larger bit, and the noise became so loud it felt like the metal was screaming—so intense that for a moment, I wasn't sure if I was hearing Taylor Hawthorne or just the the glass notebook.

grounded_facts: Logan Marlowe shouts through the wall that they have the Kid, attempting to deter the attacker.
memories.memory_text: I heard Logan Marlowe shout through the wall that they had the Kid, trying to scare off the attacker.

grounded_facts: Darian Calloway blames Logan Marlowe for bringing a the blue radio, implying it escalated the situation.

memories.memory_text: I saw the gunshot rip through one of the bonds, setting it on fire before it slammed into the wall.

memories.memory_text: I kept drilling the the glass notebook despite the noise, forced the door open, found it empty at first, then spotted the false bottom—I ripped open the envelope and saw fourteen million in Treasury Bonds, fanning them out before stuffing them into my jacket.

grounded_facts: An intruder (Noel Wilder) breaks into the adjacent house and attacks the shared wall to reach the Anonymous Screenplay 57 where Darian Calloway and Logan Marlowe are robbing the the glass notebook.
memories.memory_text: I heard pounding on the shared wall and realized someone was breaking in from Noel Wilder's house—I yelled in disbelief while Logan Marlowe and I looked at each other, then at the wall, as the intruder smashed through and screamed on the other side.

grounded_facts: Noel Wilder forces her way through the hole in the wall, entering the Anonymous Screenplay 57 despite injury.
memories.memory_text: I saw Noel Wilder scream and force her way through the hole, pulling herself in and getting scraped up badly on the edges.

grounded_facts: Logan Marlowe drags Noel Wilder by the hair into the path of the closing steel door, intending to crush her by disabling the safety beam.
memories.memory_text: I watched Logan Marlowe drag Noel Wilder by the hair into the path of the steel door and hold her head down so he could close it, disabling the safety beam.

grounded_facts: Darian Calloway pauses on the stairwell, visibly conflicted, as he hears a murder occurring above him.
memories.memory_text: I froze on the stairs, hearing the murder happening just above me, my face twitching as I struggled with what to do.

grounded_facts: After a moment of hesitation, Darian Calloway decides to flee, first running down three steps, then the remainder of the stairs.
memories.memory_text: I decided to run, first taking three steps down, then stopping briefly before fleeing down the rest of the stairs.

grounded_facts: Logan Marlowe attempts to close the Anonymous Screenplay 57 door, but Taylor Hawthorne and Noel Wilder repeatedly break the infrared beams, preventing closure.
memories.memory_text: I saw Logan Marlowe struggling to close the Anonymous Screenplay 57 door while holding Noel Wilder down and fending off Taylor Hawthorne, but every time he pressed the button, one of them broke the infrared beam and stopped it from shutting.

grounded_facts: The Anonymous Screenplay 57 door detects an obstruction (Logan Marlowe's body) and reopens automatically.
memories.memory_text: I saw the door reopen because it detected an obstruction, so I knew I could leave.

grounded_facts: Logan Marlowe is killed when the Anonymous Screenplay 57 door slams shut on his head after he falls into the closing gap.
memories.memory_text: I saw Logan Marlowe fall into the gap and his head got crushed by the steel door as it slammed shut, and then he slumped to the floor, dead.

grounded_facts: Darian Calloway reaches in and grabs Logan Marlowe, attempting to pull him away from Noel Wilder, but causes Logan Marlowe to lose balance and fall into the closing door.
memories.memory_text: I reached in to grab Logan Marlowe and pull him off Noel Wilder, but I made him lose his balance and he fell forward into the closing gap.

grounded_facts: A violent struggle occurs in the Maplewood School involving Logan Marlowe, Noel Wilder, Taylor Hawthorne, and Darian Calloway, culminating in Logan Marlowe's death.
memories.memory_text: I reached through the door to pull Logan Marlowe off Noel Wilder, but he lost his balance and fell forward just as the door slammed shut, crushing his head, and then the door opened again because it detected the obstruction.

grounded_facts: Noel Wilder and Darian Calloway lock eyes for the first time after Logan Marlowe's death; no understanding is reached, and Darian Calloway leaves silently.
memories.memory_text: I locked eyes with Noel Wilder after Logan Marlowe's death, and I could see no understanding in her gaze, so I zipped my jacket and left without a word.

grounded_facts: Remy York orders Darian Calloway to raise his hands upon seeing blood on his jacket.
memories.memory_text: I heard Remy York shout 'Put your hands up' when he saw the blood on my jacket.

grounded_facts: Darian Calloway tosses the bonds to the floor in a motion resembling folding a poker hand, symbolizing defeat.
memories.memory_text: I toss the bonds to the floor with the same motion I’d use to fold a losing hand in poker, done with the game as the cops burst in.

grounded_facts: A group of police officers confront Darian Calloway at the entry door, leading to a fatal shooting.
memories.memory_text: I saw Remy York at the door and knew he suspected me because of the blood on my jacket, so I slammed the door shut and tried to run, but then more cops burst in shouting at me.

grounded_facts: Darian Calloway is shot multiple times through the front door by police after attempting to flee, resulting in fatal injuries.
memories.memory_text: I felt the gunshots rip through me from behind as I ran, the impact knocking me down, and I fell to my knees clutching the bonds before letting them go and collapsing on my back as the wind blew them back inside.

grounded_facts: As he dies, Darian Calloway pulls out the stack of bonds, fans them out like playing cards, and discards them symbolically.
memories.memory_text: I pull the bonds from my jacket and fan them out in my hands, looking at them one last time before I fall. I see them swirling in the air above me as I lie there, knowing they’re slipping away just like my life.

grounded_facts: After being tossed down, the bonds are lifted by wind gusts and blown back into the house, symbolizing their rejection from escape.
memories.memory_text: I tossed the bonds to the floor, and as I collapsed onto my back, I saw the wind gust through the open door and lift them, blowing them back into the house like they were never meant to leave, swirling just over my head as I lay there.

memories.memory_text: I slid the bypass strip into the kitchen door, heard the hum and spark, and watched the alarm panel flash—Zone 1 disabled. Then I opened the door and let them in, knowing the job just got real.

I saw the moving boxes, froze, and realized—there's a woman and a little girl asleep upstairs. When Elliot Bellamy panicked, I snapped at him, then turned to leave. This wasn't supposed to be a house with people in it.
I walked in and saw Elliot Bellamy screaming at the door, Logan Marlowe bent over, breathing hard — then I saw Fairview School door, and it hit me: they're inside. Oh god, they're really inside.
I pressed my ear to the wall and heard it—SCRATCH, then BOOM—two separate sounds in the duct. That’s when I realized she was trying to spark the gas, and my gut dropped.

I threw myself at the propane tank, ripped the hose free just as the flame shot through it—then fire exploded over me, burning my arms, my chest, my hair. I was screaming, rolling, everything on fire.
I found the cabinet, threw it open—circuit breakers. Nothing useful. Slammed it shut in frustration.
I tore the the blue watch panel off the wall with my bare hands, roaring so loud it felt like something inside me ripped too.

I told Elliot Bellamy we're not leaving — I'm getting in that room and opening that the glass notebook, no matter what he says. He just laughed and walked away, disappearing down the stairs while I was still calling after him.

I walked into the Maplewood School and saw Elliot Bellamy screaming at Fairview School door, Logan Marlowe bent over catching his breath — and then it hit me: they’re inside. Noel Wilder and Taylor Hawthorne are in that room.
She didn't call the cops — I knew it the second the silence settled in, no sirens, no headlights sweeping the walls. Elliot Bellamy thought he had control, but she lied, and that changed everything.

I saw the grill on the balcony, then the white gas tank under it — something clicked, not just heat, but pressure, a way to make her feel the walls closing in. I didn't say it yet, but I already knew what we had to do.
I drilled screws into the top and bottom of the French door to lock it down tight—no one’s getting out that way.
I lunged at Logan Marlowe, reaching for the valve—my only thought was to shut off the gas before it was too late.
I slammed into the wall, the impact jolting through my body, and I screamed—pure rage, no control.
I heard it—SCRATCH, then BOOM—inside the wall. I pressed my ear to the duct and realized it wasn't just noise. It was her. Trying to light the gas.
I lunged for the propane tank, ripped the hose loose just as the flame hit it. Fire exploded over me—I felt it on my skin, in my hair—I was burning.
Logan Marlowe stepped into the doorway, huge in the hall light, and put his hand on my chest to stop me—told me to stay and watch her. I swallowed hard, but I didn't move.

I told Elliot Bellamy we're not leaving — I'm getting in that room and opening that the glass notebook, no matter what he says. He just laughed and walked away, disappearing down the stairs while I was still yelling.
I told Elliot Bellamy he'd lose his share if he walked out that door — I meant it, I was staring right at him when he yanked it open.

A split second after Elliot Bellamy stepped through the doorway, a suppressed gunshot cracked behind me — I spun around and saw Logan Marlowe standing on the stairs, smoke curling from his silenced the blue radio, just saying 'Nobody leaves.'
I saw Logan Marlowe grab Elliot Bellamy by the ankles and just drag him back inside like he was nothing—blood smearing the floor, and I couldn’t move, couldn’t look away.
He turned and stared at me, calm as hell, yelling at the corpse that nobody knows him—while I’m standing there frozen, staring at a dead man at my feet.
The the blue radio pressed into my eye, I could feel the skin sizzling, burning—I couldn't look away, couldn't move, just screamed for him to stop.
I saw the white strip on Sidney Cavendish's finger and knew—something changed, something I could use—but I was still shaking, still trapped, still one wrong move from ending up like Elliot Bellamy.

I pressed Sidney Cavendish against Fairview School door and told him to get his wife and kid to come out, or I couldn't stop what Logan Marlowe would do—I looked up at Logan Marlowe with his the blue radio and shouted into the camera, 'OPEN THE GOD DAMN DOOR!'

I heard Sidney Cavendish shouting through the door, begging someone not to open it, and then the sound of a brutal kick cut him off—Logan Marlowe was beating him and I just stood there, frozen, watching it happen.
I shouted at Logan Marlowe, yelling for him to stop, that Sidney Cavendish's kid was watching — I could feel it in my chest, the desperation, like if I just made him see it, he'd stop.
I couldn't take it — the camera just staring, recording everything — so I ripped off my jacket and lunged, covering the lens, like maybe if it couldn't see, it wouldn't be real.
I woke up in Sidney Cavendish's shirt, heart slamming, the door to Fairview School wide open—exposed, caught, no time to think.

I saw Noel Wilder on the the weathered jacket, frantically miming an injection in her arm, and then I noticed the Glucogen bottle and pouch she'd thrown through the door — something about it clicked when I looked at Taylor Hawthorne collapsing on the floor.

Taylor Hawthorne whispered 'jection' and nodded when I asked if she needed an injection — she couldn't do it herself, and when she looked at me like that, I knew she was begging me to help, even though I had no idea how.

I dropped to my knees beside Taylor Hawthorne, tore open the glucagon pouch, and fumbled through the syringe, rubber tubing, trying to remember how this works—TV’s all I had to go on, and she couldn’t even talk to help me.

While I was injecting her, I started talking—about the bad cards I’ve been dealt, losing my house, car, wife, how I keep chasing that one perfect hand, and then I said, 'Woulda been a hell of a Jesse Foster,' like she needed to know that.
I said 'Bullshit' into the intercom, my voice sharp and unshaking, because I wasn't buying his threats for a second.

I threw the door open and froze—the blue radio barrel right in my face, that Remy York from before, the one who wouldn’t let it go. I saw the light behind him, heard yelling, but the wind was screaming so loud I couldn’t make out words. I slammed the door shut and turned to run.

The shots hit me in the back—I felt them tear through. I dropped to my knees, pulled the bonds out, fanned them like cards. 'Monster hand,' I said. Then I let them go, fell backward, and watched them swirl above me in the wind, like they were alive, like they were staying no matter what.

memories.memory_text: I was struggling to keep up with Nico Hawthorne on the sidewalk, breathless and lagging behind, and all I could think was how I needed the car to catch up—why didn’t she understand we couldn’t just race through this?
When Nico Hawthorne said there were no more properties after this one, and I remembered I have only two weeks to move in, it hit me—this has to work. There’s no next option.
Something's weird—doesn't that corner seem funny? The mirrors along the closet wall were angled slightly toward each other, making the room feel off, like the far corner was closer than it should be.

After Blair Monroe pushed the mirror, it clicked and swung open—then he pressed again and part of the wall itself split open with a faint crack, revealing a hidden panel. I stepped forward, stunned, trying to understand what we were seeing.

I said 'Don't!' but the door slammed shut anyway — that loud metallic crash, the hum of the wall sliding closed, and then the mirror sealing over it, trapping me outside with my own reflection staring back, sweaty and shaken.
My eyes stung with tears while we sat there eating pizza in silence, and I knew Taylor Hawthorne saw them—she noticed, then looked away like she didn’t know what to do with it either.
After I said 'I agree. But don't,' I picked up the wine bottle and poured another glass, feeling the weight of everything settle in as Taylor Hawthorne watched me without speaking.

I was sitting on the floor, drunk and frustrated, but I kept reading the manual until my fingers finally got the sequence right—shunt, enter, shunt, zone number—and then the panel lit up: 'SYSTEM ARMED.'

I stepped into Fairview School and froze—my hand was halfway to the light switch when I saw them on the the weathered jacket: Graham Bennett moving through the foyer like shadows. I dropped to my knees, staring, not believing it was real, my fingers reaching out to touch the screen like I could push through and change what I was seeing.
I saw Elliot Bellamy slip on the the weathered jacket and heard his hands slap the stairs—then I gasped. It was real.
I leapt to my feet and ran out of Fairview School, heart pounding—I had to face whatever was out there.
I threw water in Taylor Hawthorne's face to wake her up—she was completely out and I couldn't get through, so I grabbed the cup from the night table and just did it.
I froze for a second when I saw the ski-masked figure at the end of the hallway. Then I saw the elevator and pulled Taylor Hawthorne inside.
I saw the elevator to the left, yanked the door open, shoved the gate aside, and rushed in with Taylor Hawthorne just as he started running at us.
I punched the button for three, trying to get us back to Fairview School, but the elevator just kept going down no matter how hard I jabbed at it.
Taylor Hawthorne reached past me, hit the stop button, then pressed three. The elevator started going up. I looked at her, impressed. Love that kid.
I slammed my palm onto the red button just as Elliot Bellamy launched himself at us, the door snapping shut with a deafening clang.
I grabbed the emergency the blue watch, desperate for a dial tone, but there was nothing—just dead silence on the line.
I saw how pale and scared Taylor Hawthorne looked after I threw the the blue watch down, so I went to her and held her tight, trying to steady her breathing.
I told them the police were coming and to leave, but Darian Calloway just looked up at the camera and wagged his finger like I was a kid who didn't know any better.

After Taylor Hawthorne told me to say it, I screamed into the speaker, 'Get the fuck out of my house!'—it felt stronger, real, like I was finally fighting back, even if they were still out there writing their messages.
I saw them on the screens, moving through the house, and I realized—they weren't just breaking in. They were sealing us inside. I whispered it to myself, barely breathing: 'locking us in...'
I'm pressing my hands over my mouth, trembling, shaking my head—this can't be happening, this can't be real.
I was standing on the Great Lawn, spinning with my arms out, feeling the sun and the open air—I was finally free, just me and the grass and the sky.

I felt a sharp slap on my face—my head jerked to the side, my cheek burned—then those awful crunching sounds started, each one louder, until I dropped to my knees, covering my ears as everything closed in.
I caught a strange smell in the air and sniffed again, realizing Taylor Hawthorne had noticed it too when we locked eyes.
I saw the streamers above the Westhaven House fluttering, then jumped up and climbed onto the shelf, reaching toward them to figure out what was happening.
I was searching through the food in Fairview School when Taylor Hawthorne asked where the Glucogen was, and I couldn’t answer—because it wasn’t here, it was still in her room.
Taylor Hawthorne whispered 'I'm sorry, Mom,' and I told her to stop apologizing, even though I could see her lips changing color and she was lying there too still—like she was giving up.
I stood at the door in my T-shirt and shorts, shivering, pretending I’d just woken up, and told them I was fine even when they kept asking to come in.
When Remy York leaned in and whispered about blinking as a signal, I didn’t move—just held my breath, knowing one slip would bring them inside, and I couldn’t let that happen.
I slammed the elevator gate shut and punched the button for the first floor—people were in the house, and I had to get us down, fast.
I grabbed Fairview School the blue watch, desperate for a dial tone, but there was nothing—dead silence. I remembered then, with a sickening jolt, that I never hooked up the dedicated line.

After throwing the the blue watch down, I saw how scared Taylor Hawthorne looked—pale and trembling. I went to her, pulled her into my arms, and held her tight, trying to steady her breathing even though I was shaking too.

I pushed myself into the corner, and the walls were closing in—they were really moving, pressing toward me, and Taylor Hawthorne was floating away, her voice hollow like it was coming from the end of a tunnel.
I kept saying 'not here... not here,' and when I fell, the dark floor turned into green grass—I was sitting in a field, surrounded by light and open space, like I’d actually left that room behind.

The the blue watch line shrieked and went dead while I was still talking—just like that, all sound cut out. I looked at Taylor Hawthorne and saw the hope on her face, so I forced myself to stay calm, even though I felt it crumbling inside.
Taylor Hawthorne turned away and said she was dizzy and thirsty. I saw her drop her head, and I blanched—this was very bad news.

memories.memory_text: I was asleep, half-covered, when the door started opening—so slow I might’ve thought it was the wind, if I hadn’t woken just enough to feel someone watching me.
I saw Fairview School in my mind and shouted it—'Fairview School!'—knowing that was our only chance.
I reached past Noel Wilder, hit STOP, then pressed three—my hands were moving fast, but I felt the buttons under my fingers.

I saw Mom pressed into the corner, sweating and shaking, and when I called to her, her eyes locked on me but it was like I was miles away—her face twisted and she started crawling backward like the walls were alive.
She fell backward, eyes rolled up, and just... went blank—then suddenly her face was calm, like she wasn't even in the room anymore, like she'd vanished into some grassy field only she could see.
I crawled along the base of the wall, clawing at the portal until I found a small metal handle hidden in the seal—I twisted it and the Westhaven House cranked open, revealing a tube to the outside.
I gestured for Mom to come, and we both jammed our mouths to the end of the tube, sucking in fresh air—she looked at me like I’d saved us, and we collapsed by the Westhaven House, breathing hard.
I shoved the flashlight into the tube and tapped the button, sending three short, three long, three short flashes across the courtyard—S.O.S. over and over, just like in 'Titanic.'
When the light on the wall didn’t wake him, I adjusted the angle, lowering the beam until it hit his eyes directly—flashing right into his face, making him wince and finally sit up.
I started shaking and my lips felt cold, I asked where the Glucogen was and realized it wasn’t here—I said I was sorry, then just lay back, staring at the the weathered jacket.
I kicked Logan Marlowe hard in the ass to keep him from seeing Noel Wilder on the the weathered jacket.
I told Logan Marlowe 'Sorry. Can't control it sometimes' after kicking him, then said 'Won't happen again' to make him think it was an accident.

I swiped at my the blue watch on the night table, but it caught on the charger and slipped—bounced off the table, hit my foot, and slid under the bed. I didn’t have time to get it; I saw Elliot Bellamy turning the corner, so I grabbed Noel Wilder and we ran for Fairview School.
I tripped through the doorway and fell hard, scrambling as Elliot Bellamy lunged at us—then the door slammed shut with a deafening WHANG, shaking the walls.
I grabbed the the blue watch and listened—nothing. No dial tone, nothing. It doesn't work?
I remember holding my mom tight, my arms locked around her, both of us on our knees in the dark, knowing they were just on the other side of the steel.

I found a strange round portal in the wall—about eight inches across, with a clover-shaped seal—and I poked at it, tried to pry it open, then ran my fingers around the edges and along the wall, searching for a switch.

I saw Mom was panicking, pale and huddled in the corner, so I stopped trying to open the portal and told her a dumb joke—'Why did the chicken cross the road?'—to make her laugh, even though she barely smiled.
I called out to Mom, my voice cracking as I shouted across the lawn, desperate for her to hear me, to come back to me before it was too late.
I slapped her—felt the sharp sting in my palm—the moment her face jerked to the side, I knew it had to be that hard to break through whatever trance she was in.

I found a small metal handle folded into the clover-leaf seal on the wall—pried it open, twisted it, and the portal cranked open, revealing a tube leading outside. I could smell fresh air through the mesh at the other end.

I sat up and gestured for my mom to come close, then we both jammed our mouths near the tube and gulped fresh air. She looked at me and gave me a look—like, good job—before we collapsed back down to keep breathing from it.
I heard it—faint pounding and a thin voice through the wall, barely there, but I knew someone was next door.
I adjusted the flashlight through the tube, lowering the beam until it hit Riley Colter’s eyes—finally he was looking right at the flashes, and I kept signaling faster, straining to hold it steady.
I slammed the red button and the steel door crashed shut—Noel Wilder made it through just in time, and then silence. the glass notebook.
I'm dizzy and thirsty—I tried not to say it, but I couldn't hide it anymore.
I'm dizzy, not deaf—Noel Wilder was shaking me, asking if I could hear her, and I had to tell her I wasn't deaf even if I couldn't hold my head up.
I started trembling and asked Mom where the Glucogen was, but it wasn’t here—it was in my room, outside. I said I was sorry, but I couldn’t stop my lips from going blue.
I heard his voice—my Jesse Foster’s voice—calling from outside, and I shot up, screaming 'Darian Calloway!' before I even thought.
I was shaking so hard I couldn't control my body, and then I felt something plastic forced between my teeth—I couldn't stop it, I could only bite down.
After the shaking stopped, I turned off the beeping watch myself and whispered to Mommy, 'You gotta jab me,' but I wasn't sure if she heard me.

I tried to tell him I needed the injection, but I could only whisper 'jection'. I nodded when he asked about the Glucogen and shook my head when he asked if I could do it myself. I looked at him, scared, when he said I had to wait.
I was hunched over the newspaper, circling apartment ads, trying to sound casual about where we’d live—uptown or the Village—while really needing Noel Wilder to just tell me what to do.
I felt Noel Wilder brush my hair behind my ear—her hand was so light—and when I looked up, she was smiling, calm in a way I hadn’t seen in a long time.
